subject: mathematics
question_text: Prove that (cosh x − sinh x)ⁿ = cosh(nx) − sinh(nx).

mark_split.label: Simplify the right side and compare

steps.label: Simplify the left side
steps.margin_note: First mark. With a minus between them the eˣ terms cancel instead, leaving e⁻ˣ — the opposite of the (cosh x + sinh x)ⁿ version, which leaves eˣ.
steps.memory_tip: With a MINUS between them the eˣ terms cancel, leaving e⁻ˣ — the opposite of the plus version, which leaves eˣ.
lines: (the eˣ terms cancel and the e⁻ˣ terms add to 2e⁻ˣ)

recall.must_convey: That cosh x − sinh x = e⁻ˣ because the eˣ terms cancel, so the left side is e⁻ⁿˣ.
accept: cosh minus sinh is e to the minus x because the positive exponentials cancel so the left side is e to the minus n x
this time the e to the x terms cancel leaving e to the minus x
the left side becomes e to the minus n x
cosh minus sinh ante e power minus x
the minus makes the other pair cancel
heard_as: e to the minus n x

steps.why: Which pair cancels depends on the sign between them. A plus cancels the e⁻ˣ terms, a minus cancels the eˣ ones — that is the entire difference between this and the (cosh x + sinh x)ⁿ version.
common_mistakes: Copying the (cosh x + sinh x)ⁿ version and writing eˣ.
Distributing the minus over only one term of the second bracket.

steps.label: Simplify the right side and compare
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The right side simplifies the same way with nx, giving e⁻ⁿˣ, and the two agree.
steps.memory_tip: The right side simplifies the same way with nx, giving e⁻ⁿˣ. Then say the two sides agree.

lines.text: (the same definitions with nx in place of x)

recall.must_convey: That the right side also collapses to e⁻ⁿˣ, so both sides agree.
accept: the right side is also e to the minus n x so both sides agree
cosh n x minus sinh n x is e to the minus n x
both sides come to the same thing
right side kuda e power minus n x, rendu equal
from one and two they are equal
heard_as: e to the minus n x

steps.why: Taken with the plus version, the two results say (cosh x + sinh x)ⁿ = eⁿˣ and (cosh x − sinh x)ⁿ = e⁻ⁿˣ — a short fact to remember, since it makes both proofs quick.
common_mistakes: Never stating that the two sides agree.
Losing the minus in the exponent.

insider_note: Simplify the bracket before using the power: cosh x − sinh x is simply e⁻ˣ. Expanding it with the binomial theorem is much longer.
